prize_parts.citation: For a visionary, densely patterned body of Romanian-language prose, with poetry as its foundation, that turns memory, the body and dream into an inner cosmos of rare formal ambition.

statement.case_for: My configuration does not change after the exchange. I still propose Cărtărescu (B011) as the single credited writer, but I now word the citation more narrowly. Under the common criteria, the voice is distinctive and recognisable: dense, patterned prose that treats memory, the body and dream as one imaginative system. Public knowledge of Blinding, the first volume of the Orbitor project, and of Solenoid points to formal architecture and intellectual depth at large scale. The structure reads as cumulative rather than merely long, and it extends a European line of encyclopedic and oneiric fiction without being derivative of it. The major works already exist, so the oeuvre can be assessed as a whole. Round 1 sharpened the citation scope. Several colleagues, Carlberg, Sem-Sandberg and Sward among them, would centre the citation on the prose and name the poetry as foundation or context. I agree, and my citation now says so. The poetry and essays remain part of the oeuvre, but I cannot show that they carry the award, and the citation should not claim more than the evidence supports. The attribution is clean: one writer, one language, one coherent project. I rest this on literary grounds. The identical opening rankings are not an argument, and I do not count them as one.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged and unresolved by the exchange. The achievement is tied to the rhythm, syntax and density of Romanian, and none of us can verify how much survives translation. The chair's question about whether the later volumes advance the project or only enlarge it has not been answered. Olsson reads them as extension, while Mattson, Sem-Sandberg and Sward hold that provisionally, and I can add no verified reading of the later volumes. I should say plainly that I cannot supply the concrete volume-by-volume evidence the chair asks for. If scale proved to hide loss of control, the case for sustained quality would weaken. In that case a more compact or more formally radical oeuvre might deserve priority. My knowledge of the poetry, essays and early work is thinner than my knowledge of the major novels. I have not independently verified any source.

responses.point: In round 1 Olsson ranked Can Xue lower than I did, because from translated selections he cannot tell whether her later work deepens the dream-logic method or repeats it. He said he would revise if I could name works that show development, and the chair's questions repeat this request.
responses.response: I cannot honestly meet that request. I can point to Frontier and Love in the New Millennium as representative works from the shortlist. Public knowledge of those titles does not let me show that her method develops, rather than only persists, across decades. I will not invent a developmental narrative to defend my second-place ranking. That is why Can Xue stays an alternative and not my preference. I accept his framing that sustained quality is the criterion on which her case is least demonstrated. I still value the radical originality of her voice. The case for her would need a reader who knows the Chinese-language corpus to argue development concretely, and that argument has not been made in this exchange.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg accepts that Cărtărescu's late work extends the project, but only provisionally. He would anchor the citation in the prose project, where the architecture is visible even in translation, and would not rest it on any single late novel. He also moved Can Xue up in his own thinking, while asking for a concrete case of development within her mode.
responses.response: I agree with him on both points, and they shaped my revised citation. Anchoring in the whole prose structure is more defensible than relying on a late volume that none of us has verified. It also keeps the citation honest about what we know. We share the same open question about Can Xue. I cannot give him the concrete case of development either, as I said to Olsson. His point that a multi-volume structure at least shows a visible pattern of accumulation is a fair asymmetry of evidence. It is not proof of quality, and I do not treat it as proof. I would stop short of saying that translated reception shows the prose holds up in the original.

responses.point: Carlberg revises her opening and favours a prose-centred citation that names the poetry as part of the oeuvre without resting the award on it. She is less persuaded than I am by Michon, since she sees a slim corpus whose achievement is largely stylistic as a harder fit for a whole-oeuvre citation.
responses.response: I accept her argument on citation scope, and my wording now follows it. On Michon I partly hold my ground. The compression and linguistic control are real, and I ranked him fourth for that reason. But I concede the substance of her objection. A small corpus can support a whole-oeuvre judgment, but I have not shown that Michon's does in terms of breadth and sustained development. That is why he is not among my two alternatives. On Adonis, I note her earlier caveat that the essays should support the poems and not carry the case. That still seems to me the right test, and I have not seen it met from the poems themselves.

responses.point: Sward places Can Xue behind Cărtărescu because of an asymmetry of evidence. Cărtărescu's multi-volume structure offers visible stages of development, while the partial translated Can Xue corpus does not. She presents this as a difference in available evidence, not in her estimate of quality.
responses.response: I find that distinction useful and I adopt it. My reason for putting Cărtărescu first is partly that his development can be described from public knowledge of the major works. I do not mean that his achievement is greater than hers in some verified sense. I should be explicit that this is a judgment about evidence, and a committee with better access to the Chinese originals could weigh it differently. It also means my first alternative is a considered fallback and not a near tie. If the question of repetition within her mode were answered favourably, the comparison could move.

uncertainties: How much of the sentence-level achievement of Cărtărescu's Romanian prose survives translation, and whether translated coverage of the poetry, essays and early work is adequate.
Whether the later volumes of the multi-part works and the later novels advance the project or only enlarge it. I cannot answer the chair's question with verified reading.
How the poetry should weigh in the citation. I have chosen prose-centred wording because I cannot show that the poetry carries the award.
Whether Can Xue's sustained single mode develops or repeats across a large, only partly translated corpus.
How a citation should define Carson's oeuvre given her translations, adaptations and performance pieces, and whether the remaining original body of work supports sustained quality.
Whether the late poetry of Adonis keeps its force independently of his influence as critic and anthologist, given the limits of judging Arabic prosody in translation.

My judgments rest on public knowledge of representative works. I have not read the corpora independently or verified any source, and agreement among the round-1 files is not independent evidence of merit.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: none apparent from the supplied profile as a connection to any shortlisted writer. My documented connections remain election alongside David Håkansson, collaboration with Kate Larson, my biography of Selma Lagerlöf, and committee colleagues. None involves a shortlisted candidate. My 2024 Nobel Prize Museum interview was given on behalf of the committee and does not establish a personal preference. My own practice as a novelist and biographer is literary context and not evidence for a candidate. The members' conflict statements in the round-1 files are their own readings of supplied profiles, and I do not adjudicate them. These runs disclose conflicts and do not rule on them.
